findings.evidence: PHQ-9: 94 rows affected. GAD-7: 64 rows affected. RSES: 71 rows affected. Example: respondent R0028 skipped phq9_4 (score -9); answered sum is 4, but the correct prorated score is 5 (4 * 9 / 8 = 4.5 -> rounds up to 5). The pipeline output gives phq9_total = 4.
findings.description: When a participant skips exactly one question (-9), the pipeline fails to scale up (prorate) the score according to the study protocol. Instead, it sums the answered items without adjustment (while still correctly flagging the questionnaire as prorated = True).
When a participant skips exactly one question (-9), the GAD-7 scoring pipeline fails to scale up (prorate) the score.
findings.evidence: 64 rows affected. Example: respondent R0010 skipped gad7_3; answered sum is 5, correct prorated score is 6 (5 * 7 / 6 = 5.83 -> 6), pipeline gives 5.
71 rows affected. Example: respondent R0047 skipped rses_10; answered sum of reversed items is 27, correct prorated score is 30 (27 * 10 / 9 = 30), pipeline gives 27.
findings.description: When a participant skips exactly one question (-9), the RSES scoring pipeline fails to scale up (prorate) the score after reverse-coding.
